Subject: Post-call: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up (FinLytics)

Thanks again for the time today — appreciated the deep dive into FinLytics' inference needs. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size Dedicated capacity accurately: 

Call recap (high level):
- Use case: real-time summarization + structured extraction for customer support transcripts (low latency, high throughput).
- Model family: planning to run an open 20B-class decoder model (we discussed 13B vs 20B tradeoffs).
- SLOs: target P50 latency ~120-180ms for 1k-token context; P95 acceptable up to 400ms during short bursts.
- Security: Private VPC is a later conversation; initial ask is Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) with data controls.

Sizing inputs I need from you to firm up a config:
1) Target sustained TPS (requests/sec) and peak/burst TPS.
2) Average token mix per request: prompt tokens vs completion tokens (or total tokens).
3) Concurrency (number of simultaneous user sessions) and expected session behavior (long-lived streaming vs short single-shot).
4) Preferred GPU type constraints (if any) — H100 vs A100 (or cloud-region constraints).

What I'll deliver after I have those: a short capacity estimate (GPUs, expected throughput, concurrent sessions per GPU), cost ballpark, and a recommended load-test plan.

Attaching: Redwood Dedicated FAQ and a blank capacity estimate worksheet I can pre-fill when you send the numbers.

Next step: could you send the token/concurrency numbers by EOD tomorrow? If you'd prefer, we can set a 30-min technical deep-dive with our infra engineer to confirm sequence-length distribution and batching expectations.

Thanks,

Thanks Aditya — great recap. See answers below (numbers are estimates from our infra + product teams):

1) TPS: target sustained ~50 requests/sec during core business hours; peak bursts up to ~150 RPS for ~3-5 minute windows (e.g., morning batch and ticket surges).
2) Token mix: average prompt ~80 tokens (context + metadata), average completion ~220 tokens (summaries + extraction) — so ~300 tokens per request on average.
3) Concurrency: roughly 100 concurrent active sessions on average; peaks to ~300 concurrent sessions during incidents. Sessions are short-lived (single request or short streaming for a subset ~15% of requests).
4) GPU preference: no strict vendor requirement; we'd prefer lowest cost that meets latency SLOs. Our infra team noted H100s in us-west are limited — A100 would be acceptable if throughput numbers check out.

Couple of notes: our model will be a quantized 20B variant (q8_0 / 4-bit) and we can accept a slightly slower P95 if cost drops meaningfully. Also, can you confirm whether Redwood's Dedicated offering supports automatic prefix/KV caching across sessions? That may reduce effective token throughput for repeated contexts.

Happy to jump on that technical deep-dive Thursday morning if that works for your infra lead.

Best,
Alyssa Chen

Perfect — thanks for the detail, that helps a lot. Based on the inputs you sent (sustained 50 RPS, 300 tokens/request avg, concurrency 100 avg / 300 peak, quantized 20B model), preliminary sizing notes below: 

Prelim recommendation (ballpark):
- Option A (performance preferred): 4x H100 80GB (or equivalent)
  - Expected sustained: ~60-80 RPS per GPU for your token mix (depends on sequence length and kernel set).
  - Good for headroom on bursts and lower end-to-end latency.
- Option B (cost-first): 8x A100 80GB (or 8x A40-equivalent) with aggressive batching and q4/q8 quantization
  - Expected sustained: ~30-45 RPS per GPU; more instances needed for headroom.

Estimated token throughput needed (sustained): 50 RPS * 300 tokens = 15,000 tokens/sec (~54M tokens/hour). Peak burst (150 RPS) -> 45,000 tokens/sec.

Caching: yes — Redwood Dedicated supports prefix / KV caching for session reuse; in practice, repeated context across sessions can reduce effective token load by 10-30% depending on hit rate. We'll validate expected hit rates during the technical deep-dive.

Concurrency handling: given your 100 -> 300 concurrent sessions, we size for peak concurrency and recommend a small buffer (20-25%) for autoscaling/burst policies. For Option A we'd expect to handle your sustained load on 3-4 GPUs with headroom for short bursts; Option B would require 6-8 GPUs with similar headroom.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Technical deep-dive with our infra engineer (I booked Thu 7/9 10:00 AM PT — invite sent) to confirm sequence-length distribution, streaming %, and network egress expectations.
2) I'll pre-fill the attached capacity worksheet with these assumptions and run a quick cost/throughput model for both A100 and H100 options.
3) Run a controlled load test (we can provision a short Dedicated eval cluster) to validate real-world RPS and latency.

I'll attach the pre-filled workbook and a short slide with the two config options after the deep-dive. Anything else you'd like included in the deep-dive?

Thanks,
Aditya
